reuse.why: Works inside the existing getNextDate and its RSchedule occurrences, but does not put the daily rule where the weekend rule is shared (getDateWithSkippedWeekend or the recurrence config), so other weekend-handling callers do not get it.

duplication.why: No copied block; the daily check is written once, though it reads frequency from dateCond.value while the rest of the function reads value.schedule.data.

placement.why: The rule is placed in getNextDate only, while getUpcomingDates in server/schedules/app.ts and createScheduleList in server/budget/schedule-template.ts apply weekend handling themselves via getDateWithSkippedWeekend and keep moving daily weekend occurrences.

scope.why: One change in getNextDate and one parameterised test; nothing unrelated.

maintainability.why: The daily-skip rule now lives in one of three weekend-handling paths, so the schedule's upcoming-dates list and budget templates disagree with getNextDate, and a re-query loop per weekend day is harder to reason about than excluding the days in the recurrence.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Uses the existing getNextDate/RSchedule path; it does not route around an existing abstraction, it just does not cover the other callers.

one_place.where: Changed only in getNextDate (packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts); getUpcomingDates (server/schedules/app.ts) and createScheduleList (server/budget/schedule-template.ts) still apply getDateWithSkippedWeekend to daily occurrences.
